column2: The foreigners take God's ark from Abennezer to Azotus; inherited Ebenezer and Ashdod remain declared conventional name forms, without changing the route or actor.
The repeated taking and bringing of the Lord's ark into Dagon's house precedes its placement beside Dagon; both named objects remain explicit.

Early entry, seeing and the presentative fallen Dagon lead to restoration; the entire additional hand/torment/buttocks passage remains in this stored unit. There was supplies the deictic force of idou after looked.
column3: Hedrai here is rendered anatomically as buttocks; this does not establish a specific diagnosis.

column2: The severed head, both soles of hands, each front part of amapheth, fallen wrists and remaining back are all retained. Only is supported by plen rather than added exclusivity.
column3: The odd bodily descriptions and amapheth remain opaque; no reconstructed statue anatomy or alternative source reading is silently supplied.

column2: The prohibition on stepping upon Dagon's step contrasts with the emphatic stepping over it; priests and everyone entering, Ashdod and to this day remain.
column3: Always represents the ongoing customary action in context, not a separate Greek frequency adverb; a more formally emphatic alternative is they do step over it.

column2: The heavy divine hand, outbreak into the ships, mice in the territory and great deadly turmoil remain. Affliction supplies the unstated object of brought in the disease context.
column3: The subject and physical sense of exezesen remain difficult; it broke out is an interpretive English construction, and ships is not emended to another body part.

column2: The men's refusal to keep the ark follows their observation; the harsh hand is upon both us and Dagon our god, preserving their own explanation.
Sending, gathering the satraps, their question, the Gathites' invitation and the ark's actual transfer are separately retained. Human speakers address one another with ordinary pronouns.
The very great turmoil accompanies the Lord's hand; small through great, bodily striking and the Gathites' making seats all remain.
column3: The repeated hedrai is translated buttocks and seats according to syntax; the exact medical or practical relationship remains unresolved.

column2: Ashkelon is repeated as destination and inhabitants' identity; their question retains killing us and our people rather than substituting Ekron from another tradition.

The imperative return of the ark, its settling in its place and the emphatic negative expectation of death remain within the speakers' request. The following explanation retains the whole city's heavy deadly turmoil and the entry of the ark.
Alive and not dead are both retained before bodily striking; the city's cry ascends to heaven without an added response or diagnosis.
Seven months in the foreigners' country and the land's producing mice both remain; teemed expresses the outbreak image in readable English.
Priests, diviners and enchanters remain three groups. Their question concerns what to do with the ark and in what to return it; no vehicle has yet been specified.

The conditional sending, prohibition on an empty return, emphatic repayment for torment, healing and propitiation for you remain. The final negative fear clause preserves the risk that the hand might not withdraw.
column3: Something supplies the object implicit in the repayment expression; the ritual category and me ouk clause need specialist review, rather than automatic substitution of a familiar guilt-offering formula.

column2: The reply specifies five gold seats according to the satraps and one affliction shared by you, rulers and people; it continues into the mice instruction in verse 5.
Gold mice reproduce the destructive mice, followed by giving glory and the purpose of a lighter hand upon people, gods and land. The repeated three beneficiaries remain.
column3: Lighten His hand upon expresses relief from its weight; Greek apo marks removal from each, so a closer alternative would retain from explicitly.

column2: The question repeats heaviness of hearts and compares Egypt and Pharaoh; God's mocking them precedes sending away and departure. The unnamed objects remain pronouns rather than added identities.
A new cart and two first-calving cows without their young are required, followed by yoking and taking the calves home; no never-yoked qualification is inserted.
The ark, gold repayment objects and deposit bersechthan stay distinct, as do sending, driving off and going away. The opaque term is retained beside its provisional category.
column3: The relationship of thema and bersechthan, and the several feminine pronoun antecedents, remain open; no modern container type is asserted.

column2: The watchers' conditional test follows the road toward Beth-shemesh: His agency if it goes there, otherwise a denial that His hand touched them and an attribution to chance. This is the speakers' proposed test.
The foreigners carry out the instruction with two first-calving cows, a cart and calves confined at home; the calf separation is not omitted as repetition.
The ark, deposit ergab and gold mice are placed on the cart; ergab is not harmonized with bersechthan in verse 8 or expanded with an absent object.
Straight travel on one path, laboring and no right or left turn remain before the satraps following to the border. Laboring follows ekopion rather than replacing it with lowing.
column3: The exact force of laboring in the cattle narrative and the singular pronoun followed it remain questions; the inherited ark/cart reference is left broad.

column2: Wheat harvesting in the valley precedes lifted eyes, sight of the ark and joy at meeting it; the crop and meeting expression remain explicit.

Hosea's field, their setting up a large stone beside the cart, splitting its wood and offering the cows as a whole burnt offering remain. The plural setting action is not replaced by a stone merely existing there.
column3: Hosea represents Osee here; it is not silently changed to Joshua.

column2: Levites bring up the ark, deposit ergab and gold objects and set them on the large stone. The men's whole burnt offerings and sacrifices are two coordinated offerings in this verse.
column3: The several feminine pronouns around the deposit and gold objects remain somewhat awkward; no unexpressed container arrangement is asserted.

column2: The five satraps see and return to Ashkelon on that day; selected destination and number remain unchanged.
The gold-seat list gives one each for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron. Ekron's presence here does not authorize replacing Ashkelon in the preceding narrative.
Gold mice correspond to all cities of the five satraps, from fortified city to the Perizzite's village and the large stone, identified by the covenant ark and Hosea's field.
column3: The boundaries of the counting formula and its extension to the stone remain syntactically difficult; no recalculated count is supplied.

column2: The sons of Jeconiah's lack of pleasure among the men because they saw the ark is retained, followed by seventy men and fifty thousand men and the people's mourning at the Lord's great blow.
column3: The negative pleasure clause and its causal connection remain open; the two figures are not conflated or corrected, and seeing is not changed to looking inside.

column2: The men ask who can pass before this holy Lord and to whom the ark shall go up away from them. Pass preserves dielthein rather than importing stand.
Messengers announce the foreigners' return of the ark and command Kiriath-jearim's inhabitants to come down and bring it up to themselves; both directions and ordinary plural human address remain.
